title: Bangladesh to get €30 million or more in Global Shield climate grants
excerpt: The money will fund flood and cyclone risk data, climate insurance for farmers and fishers, and aid released on disaster forecasts.
content:
Bangladesh will receive at least €30 million (about Tk 415 crore) in grants from the Global Shield against Climate Risks, Dr Md Saimum Parvez, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Environment, Forest and Climate Change, said at the Bangladesh Pavilion at COP31 in Antalya on Wednesday (18 November), The Business Standard reported, citing BSS.

"This is entirely a grant, not a loan," he said. The application was made through the Economic Relations Division (ERD).

The money will pay for flood and cyclone risk assessment, better data systems, climate insurance for farmers, fishers and small entrepreneurs, and fast assistance released when forecasts show a disaster is coming. A further $20 million (about Tk 250 crore) could follow if the first phase is carried out well.

Bangladesh has also been chosen to prepare an investment plan of up to $30 million under the Climate Investment Funds' ARISE programme, the report said. The Global Shield was set up by the G7 and the V20 group of climate-vulnerable countries.

Why it matters

Bangladesh has pressed at COP31 for climate finance as grants rather than loans. This is grant money for exactly the work many NGOs already do: early warning, forecast-based cash, and insurance for poor households. How it is channelled will decide whether community organisations get a share.

What to watch

Which agencies and partners will deliver the programmes, whether NGOs and local groups have a role in forecast-based payouts, and when the first money arrives.
